rationale: This board fails as a portfolio because too many options are the same box/bar chassis with repeated roof and footprint logic. The dominant lifted-block / attached-cluster language occupies roughly 6 of 16 visible candidates, or about 37.5%, which exceeds the 30% cap. Only about nine families are legible at image scale, below the required ten. The strongest candidates are the ones that actually change section and threshold: maas_01, maas_13, and maas_16. The rest are mostly minor variants of bar, carved box, or stepped monolith types. For the next run, the portfolio should be rebuilt around clearer public-space operators—courtyard, split-wing, carve, notch, lift—so the ground edge and upper massing read as a single program-specific system rather than a collection of similar boxes.

repeated_family_groups.shared_language: attached/clustered bar with front notch or lift; same broad bar chassis, only local add-ons change
carved monolith / voided bar with small puncture or notch variations; same boxy mass, different incision depth
lifted spine / elevated block with nearly identical roof and undercroft logic; variations are mostly roof finish or minor stepping
stepped or terraced block family; same mass read with only modest notch/setback changes

required_next_relations: Introduce at least one true courtyard or split-wing relation with a usable public void, not just a notch.
Push the ground floor into a clearly legible active edge: recessed, lifted, or cut so the street threshold reads as programmatic space.
Vary section logic across the portfolio: one bent mass, one lift, one carve, one terrace; avoid repeating the same box chassis.
Differentiate roofs through spatial consequence, not silhouette trimming—roof should respond to void, terrace, or split, not just step the top plane.
Keep one calm upper mass above a more active base; use upper transformations that preserve the mixed-use ground relationship.
Replace repeated bar/box variants with families that change footprint, support, and void relationship all at once.
Aim for a minimum of ten materially distinct form/spatial families by combining courtyard, notch, split, carve, terrace, lift, and bent-bar relations.
